title: Software Design
description: Can turn requirements into a modular design and change structure without changing behavior — and can defend the coupling and trade-offs that choice accepts.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can map an unfamiliar codebase's entry point and at least five modules from the code, not the README alone, and name one cohesion or coupling problem in a module — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can land a scoped change in code they did not write, cite two existing conventions by file and line, and commit a design note before any implementation.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently refactor a module behind a passing test net so behavior stays the same, and show commit-by-commit which smell each change addresses.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can write or defend a design decision that names rejected alternatives, at least one accepted negative consequence, and what would have to change for the recommendation to flip.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's module split or ADR, name a coupling or missing trade-off a mentor can point at, and teach when to evolve a running design versus rewrite it on a system they did not author.
